name: Autonomous Floor Scrubber
definition: A commercial floor-scrubbing machine that navigates an approved route autonomously while applying solution, agitating the floor and recovering liquid, with people still responsible for setup, supervision, exceptions and service.
includedScope: Operator-taught or mapped commercial scrubbers with documented autonomous operation
excludedScope: Manual scrubbers without an autonomous mode
headline: Autonomous floor scrubber navigation, safety, docking, proof-of-work and buyer verification
description: This profile separates cleaning hardware from autonomy, site approval, docking and fleet-data claims so buyers can validate the complete operating system.
metaDescription: Autonomous floor scrubber guide covering navigation, safety, docking, cleaning systems, models and procurement checks.
disclaimer: This is an independent category reference, not safety approval or model-specific purchasing advice. Validate the exact machine, software release, mapped site, supervision plan, regional conformity and service terms.

keyFacts.label: System boundary
keyFacts.value: Cleaning machine plus autonomy stack plus approved site process
keyFacts.evidence: Official sources separately describe cleaning functions, sensors, route operation and operator tasks.
keyFacts.scope: Reviewed models only; autonomy does not remove human responsibility.

keyFacts.label: Navigation
keyFacts.value: Mapped or taught routes with model-specific localization and obstacle response
keyFacts.evidence: Manufacturers describe route teaching, mapping and live obstacle handling using different technologies.

keyFacts.label: Docking
keyFacts.value: Charging is common; water refill, draining and rinsing are optional and model-specific
keyFacts.evidence: Kärcher documents an optional docking station; other reviewed machines document different charging workflows.
keyFacts.scope: Do not infer full-service docking from automatic charging.

keyFacts.label: Productivity
keyFacts.value: Theoretical, practical and autonomous-route coverage are different metrics
keyFacts.evidence: Manufacturer sources use different area-performance labels and conditions.
keyFacts.scope: Named values retain each source boundary.

systemFlow.name: Site setup
systemFlow.componentFamily: Mapping, route teaching and operating zones
systemFlow.role: Defines where and how the robot may clean.
systemFlow.evidence: Official sources describe mapped or taught cleaning plans.

systemFlow.name: Perception and localization
systemFlow.componentFamily: LiDAR, cameras, proximity and localization stack
systemFlow.role: Locates the machine and detects relevant obstacles.
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturers publish model-specific sensor and navigation descriptions.
systemFlow.scope: No universal sensor capability is inferred.

systemFlow.name: Path execution
systemFlow.componentFamily: Motion control, speed limits and obstacle response
systemFlow.role: Moves through the approved route and handles normal traffic conditions.
systemFlow.evidence: Official sources describe autonomous route execution and obstacle avoidance.
systemFlow.scope: Actual response depends on site and software.

systemFlow.name: Scrub and recovery
systemFlow.componentFamily: Solution, brush deck, squeegee and vacuum recovery
systemFlow.evidence: Product pages identify scrub and recovery systems.
systemFlow.scope: Deck, tanks and settings are configuration-specific.

systemFlow.name: Handover and support
systemFlow.componentFamily: Alerts, reports, charging, docking and exception workflow
systemFlow.role: Returns work to staff when intervention or replenishment is required.
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturers document alerts, reporting and charging or dock options.
systemFlow.scope: Connectivity and service availability vary by market.

variants.name: Teach-and-repeat scrubber
variants.operatorRelationship: Staff teach routes and handle exceptions
variants.spaceConstraints: Requires stable route geometry and validated boundaries
variants.limitations: A taught route is not a general-purpose autonomy claim.
variants.evidence: Tennant and Nilfisk describe operator-taught autonomous operation.

variants.name: Map-managed compact robot
variants.operatorRelationship: Staff create maps, dispatch work and supervise outcomes
variants.spaceConstraints: Doorways, glass, lifts and congestion require trials
variants.limitations: Compact size does not guarantee access or safety approval.
variants.evidence: Hako, Kärcher and LionsBot position compact autonomous machines for indoor sites.

variants.name: Dock-enabled system
variants.taskScale: Longer repeated operations with reduced manual replenishment
variants.operatorRelationship: Staff maintain dock, consumables and exceptions
variants.spaceConstraints: Needs utilities, docking clearance and protected access
variants.limitations: Dock functions differ: charging alone is not refill and drain.
variants.evidence: Kärcher documents an optional full-service dock.

performanceMetrics.name: Cleaning path
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Nominal width of the scrub deck
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Does not establish edge cleaning or route accessibility.

performanceMetrics.name: Area performance
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Theoretical, practical and tested values differ
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not treat maximum output as achieved autonomous coverage.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Sources label performance using different bases.

performanceMetrics.name: Runtime and charge time
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Battery, floor, settings and route dependent
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Maximum runtime is not a duty-cycle guarantee.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Manufacturers publish model-specific runtime or charging data.

performanceMetrics.name: Tank capacity
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Tank size does not establish autonomous duration.

performanceMetrics.name: Intervention rate
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Measures operational resilience in the actual site
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Must define event, distance, time and assisted recovery
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Vendor demonstrations are not normalized site results.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official sources document intervention and exception workflows but not one common metric.
performanceMetrics.scope: WCB procurement metric for a controlled site trial.

applicationFit.evidence: Manufacturers position reviewed robots for retail, transport, warehouse and public-space routes.
applicationFit.scope: Mapped indoor areas within product limits.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Best fit begins with stable routes and measurable manual exception work.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Run a representative route trial across full operating hours.

applicationFit.evidence: Reviewed models are shown or positioned in public facilities and include obstacle sensing.
applicationFit.scope: Only after local risk assessment and site approval.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Pedestrians, children, glass, temporary displays and emergency routes are decisive.
applicationFit.basis: Public-area positioning plus autonomous safety scope.
applicationFit.limitations: Sensor presence is not proof of suitability for every traffic pattern.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Test peak traffic, edge cases, signage and escalation response.

applicationFit.evidence: Vendors document reporting, charging and optional docking functions.
applicationFit.scope: Exact utilities, service plan and dock configuration.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Shift value depends on replenishment, recovery, exceptions and proof-of-work together.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Document every planned human touch and response-time owner.

componentStack.scope: Regional conformity and site approval remain required.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Achieved coverage, exceptions and recovery quality
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official metrics use different reporting boundaries.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Measure completed clean area per staffed hour, not robot motion alone.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Run timed trials and classify every intervention.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm route, deck, tanks, battery and software version.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Site safety case and traffic behavior
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Treating a certification or sensor list as site approval
procurementDecisions.evidence: IEC scope and manufacturer controls are product-level inputs.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Approve the whole operating method and exception response.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Conduct and document a site-specific risk assessment.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Test stops, glass, drops, low obstacles, blocked routes and restart rules.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Exact dock functions and utility interfaces
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Equating automatic charging with autonomous refill and drain
procurementDecisions.assessment: Value the dock only after mapping every eliminated and retained task.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Obtain utility drawings and a task-responsibility matrix.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm water, drain, power, clearance, backflow and service access.

engineeringChecks.reason: Autonomous behavior depends on current maps, permissions and releases.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Record versions, change control, rollback and map ownership.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Manufacturers document digital mapping and fleet functions.

engineeringChecks.reason: Moving machinery operates near people and property.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Verify conformity documents and site risk controls.
engineeringChecks.evidence: IEC 63327 addresses commercial automatic floor-treatment machines.

engineeringChecks.reason: Docking can introduce water, drainage, power and access interfaces.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Approve the exact installation drawings and maintenance access.

engineeringChecks.reason: Brushes, squeegees, filters, batteries and sensors determine uptime.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Obtain exact part numbers, stock plan and response SLA.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official product resources identify model-specific support systems.

standards.name: IEC 63327:2021
standards.applicability: Safety requirements for automatic floor-treatment machines for commercial use within its scope.
standards.evidence: IEC publishes the scope and relationship to relevant appliance standards.
standards.scope: Confirm regional adoption and product declaration.

standards.name: IEC 60335-2-72:2021
standards.applicability: Particular safety requirements for commercial floor-treatment machines with or without traction drive.
standards.scope: Automatic-machine additions and regional adoption must be checked.
